parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Hello, everyone. My presentation today is about the cave paintings produced by prehistoric artists about 30,000 years ago and in particular the symbols that appear in or near these paintings. These symbols are found deep in caves in many countries around the world, but the ones I’m going to talk about today are mainly European.
Firstly, a little about the most common symbols. The symbols that have been discovered are of different shapes and sizes. Some are easily recognizable as they’re quite simple. The most basic are just a series of dots, but they may also include forms such as the triangle. However, other symbols are more complex. A case in point is the wavy line. This is sometimes used on its own, but the same wavy line is also used as part of a larger picture of a horse, so we think this is what the wavy line represents.
One very important symbol is what’s called the hand symbol. This frequently appears on the walls of caves. I’ll talk about it in a bit more detail. Firstly, how it was made. The paint itself was made up from a variety of things that cave artists would have had access to. They had fire, so charcoal was one ingredient. Another was the fat from the animals they would have hunted, and lastly, the saliva from their own mouths.
Then there’s a question of how they actually applied the runny paint onto the walls of the cave. It certainly wouldn’t have been easy. They would have had to use something hollow. In fact, it’s likely to have looked like a straw, you know, like the kind we use for drinking nowadays. They’d have sucked the paint up into it, then blown it out. Researchers have recently recreated both the paint and the processes used to make the hand symbols. The artist would have first put his hand flat against the wall, then blown the paint onto the wall creating an outline of the hand. The researchers who’ve tried to recreate the process have said that not only is it a difficult technique to master, but also that a strange noise is produced. It also led them to feel light-headed, so we can only imagine that these cave artists felt the same.
I’m sure you’ll agree that these symbols are really interesting, but they’re also of vital importance. Researchers have now identified a total of 26 symbols commonly used in France and Spain. We only have this knowledge thanks to a database that’s been created, and which is being added to all the time. It clearly demonstrates that many symbols are often used in particular combinations, even if they’re in different places. This is significant, as it looks like different tribes of cave people who lived and travelled through the area at that time would have seen these markings as well as adding to them. Although researchers don’t believe that these symbols are a language as such, they are happy to call them a type of code.
There is evidence to support this idea. One sequence of five symbols is particularly common in caves in Spain. Exactly the same sequence of five symbols has been found carved into a necklace made from the teeth of a red deer. So it appears that this combination of symbols may have had a special meaning. Of course, many of these explanations are theory as opposed to hard facts, which is why there is disagreement among researchers about the significance of what we’re seeing.
One theory is called the Great Leap Forward. The idea is that around 35,000 years ago there was a sudden increase in creativity which led to the invention of the boat among other things. However, not everyone agrees. In fact, many scientists believe that what has been found in Africa seems to indicate that this increase in creativity happened much earlier, around 70 to 90,000 years ago, and more gradually. One example of an artifact that is offered to support the idea is the discovery of different sorts of arrows, which would have been used for hunting. These scientists suggest that the reason more symbols haven’t been found from this earlier time is because they would have been painted on things that did not survive, such as wood. In fact, we are very lucky that caves have protected these specimens as well as they have, or we might never have known what these artists were capable of.

analyses.content: 听到 "include forms such as"（包括诸如……的形状）这个举例信号词后，紧跟在后面的词就是答案。
The most basic are just a series of dots, but they may also include forms such as the triangle.
你可能会听到前面的 "dots"，但题目中 dots 已经给出了，要注意听 dots 后面那个并列的形状。
This is sometimes used on its own, but the same wavy line is also used as part of a larger picture of a horse, so we think this is what the wavy line represents.
不要只听到 "wavy line" 就走神，重点是它依附于哪个更大的图像（part of a larger picture）。
录音中提到 wavy line（波浪线）是 larger picture of a... 的一部分，紧接着说这就是它 "represents"（代表）的内容，答案就在代表之后。
They had fire, so charcoal was one ingredient. Another was the fat from the animals they would have hunted, and lastly, the saliva from their own mouths.
容易听到 "animals"，但 fat 是来自 animals 的提取物，fat 才是具体的配料名称。
题目问的是混合成分，录音中用 "Another was..." 介绍了除 charcoal 和 saliva 之外的中间那个成分。
They would have had to use something hollow. In fact, it’s likely to have looked like a straw, you know, like the kind we use for drinking nowadays.
你可能听到了 "hollow"（中空的），但那是形容词，题目需要填的是具体的物品名称。
题目中的 "similar to"（像……）对应录音中的 "looked like"，后面的名词就是用来吹颜料的工具。
The researchers who’ve tried to recreate the process have said that not only is it a difficult technique to master, but also that a strange noise is produced.
不要填 "light-headed"，那是吹颜料导致的身体感觉（result），而不是发出的声音。
题目中的 "unusual"（不寻常的）对应录音中的 "strange"，紧跟在其后的名词就是答案。
录音先否定了 symbols 是 language，然后转折说研究者 "happy to call them a type of..."，此处就是正确答案。
Although researchers don’t believe that these symbols are a language as such, they are happy to call them a type of code.
千万别填 "language"，录音中明确说了 "don't believe... are a language"。
Exactly the same sequence of five symbols has been found carved into a necklace made from the teeth of a red deer.
容易误填 "teeth" 或 "deer"，题目结构是 "on a [object] made from..."，teeth 是制作材料，necklace 才是那个物体。
听到 "found carved into a..."（被发现刻在……里面），这个介词短语后的物体就是承载符号的东西。
The idea is that around 35,000 years ago there was a sudden increase in creativity which led to the invention of the boat among other things.
这题定位词 "Great Leap Forward" 出现后要集中注意力听具体的发明物。
题目中的 "innovations such as"（创新，例如……）对应录音中的 "invention of"，后面的名词即为答案。
One example of an artifact that is offered to support the idea is the discovery of different sorts of arrows, which would have been used for hunting.
不要填 "hunting"，那是用途（used for hunting），不是物品本身。
题目中的 "types of" 对应录音中的 "different sorts of"，后面紧跟着的就是在这个早于预期的时间点发现的物品。
These scientists suggest that the reason more symbols haven’t been found from this earlier time is because they would have been painted on things that did not survive, such as wood.
注意题目问的是 painted on（画在什么上面），不要填成 "survive" 或 "specimens"。
录音解释了为什么更早期的符号没留下来，因为它们 "painted on things that did not survive, such as..."，例子即答案。
